# Velair 1.8.0

Velair 1.8.0 brings the work tested across the 1.8 beta series into a stable release. It adds a single-climate Lovelace card, more useful Comfort context, and schedules that can leave a device's target temperature under its own control. It also improves climate-change attribution and diagnostics.

## ✨ Added

- Added an optional, responsive single-climate Lovelace card for controlling and understanding a zone in one place. It brings together HVAC and target controls, Automatic/Manual ownership, Current state, today's timeline, Room Assist, Preconditioning, Comfort, and configurable Boost, Pause, and script actions. The card adapts to Home Assistant themes and mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.
- Schedules, Profiles, and templates can now change only the HVAC mode, including `auto`, without sending a temperature ([#29](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/29)). They can also send supported presets, fan modes, swing settings, or target humidity without a temperature or HVAC mode command ([#30](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/30)). The public `velair.set_hvac_mode` service provides mode-only control for scripts and automations.
- Expanded observational Comfort with Simple, Guided psychrometric, and Custom temperature-aware humidity ranges; Humidex, dew point, and absolute humidity; indoor/outdoor comparison; and cautious ventilation guidance. The graph follows the selected model, while the physical Environmental condition remains separate from perceived-heat context. A Ventilation opportunity sensor exposes the assessment for automations; Velair does not operate windows or change climate control based on outdoor readings.
- Added per-zone control and optional delivery diagnostics entities, plus a [sensor reference](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/blob/main/docs/user/sensors.md) with their attributes and examples ([#22](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/pull/22), [discussion #26](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/discussions/26)).
- Added a persisted target-temperature step fallback for climate entities that omit `target_temp_step`, applied consistently across schedules, Profiles, Room Assist, imports, and climate-card controls.

## 🚀 Improved

- Block editors show the selected climate options compactly and explain what a block will send inside its options panel. They warn when a target may not fit the HVAC mode active when the block runs ([#30](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/30)).
- Diagnostics now provides more context for investigating external climate changes, including the latest Velair target, delivery and settling state, and Room Assist context ([#28](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/28)).
- Contextual help uses consistent sizing and stays within the viewport on mouse, keyboard, and touch interfaces.

## 🛠️ Fixed

- Fixed delayed, intermediate, out-of-order, and Room Assist climate updates being mistaken for external manual adjustments in the cases identified during beta testing ([#28](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/28)).
- Fixed a Home Assistant thread-safety error when an unavailable climate reconnects and Velair restores its current intent ([#27](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/27)).
- Corrected Comfort freshness: repeated Home Assistant reports keep direct sensors current, while sensors that stop reporting become stale. Valid climate temperature and humidity attributes remain usable without an independent freshness timestamp; retained readings from unavailable climates and target humidity are not treated as measurements ([#32](https://github.com/cgonfer/velair/issues/32)).
- Fixed hidden Room Assist help content leaving an empty area beside the temperature graph.

## 🧭 Notes

- Existing configurations remain compatible and stored data is migrated automatically. The Environmental condition state remains compatible with existing automations. New Comfort sources and climate-card sections are optional; delivery diagnostics entities are disabled by default.
- Portable exports now use model version 12. Existing backups remain importable, but older Velair versions cannot import a new version 12 export. Keep a backup before testing a downgrade.
- Comfort's **Data freshness** section shows which direct sensors use **Stale after**. Climate attributes have no independent measurement timestamp, so their freshness is shown as unverified rather than inferred from changes to the climate target. A Home Assistant report does not prove that the physical sensor sampled again.
- Outdoor Comfort comparisons do not account for rain, wind, outdoor air quality, security, forecasts, or actual air exchange. They are informational and never open windows or change climate control.
- After updating through HACS, restart Home Assistant and refresh the browser or companion app. If the previous interface remains visible, perform a hard refresh or clear the site cache.
